model_annotation: This bar chart (Figure 2) illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between a baseline Mistral-v0.2 model and the same model further fine-tuned on each of six medical specialty datasets. The horizontal axis is labeled "Per-specialty terms" and contains six categories arranged from left to right: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents negative log-probabilities, though the specific axis label and scale values are not clearly legible in the image. For each specialty category along the horizontal axis, there is a group of multiple bars, where each bar represents the model fine-tuned on a different specialty's data. The bars within each group are color-coded, and the same color consistently represents the same fine-tuned model variant across all six category groups, indicating that each color corresponds to a particular specialty's fine-tuning data. The leftmost position before the grouped bars appears to show a baseline reference. The bars vary in height across the different per-specialty term categories and across the different fine-tuned model variants, with some groups showing more variation among their constituent bars than others. The chart does not appear to sort the bars within each group in any particular ascending or descending order, and no individual bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding or outlining. The overall purpose of the chart is to show how fine-tuning on different specialty datasets affects the model's token-level probability assignments for clinical terms associated with each of the six specialties.
